clue.text: Pale, sickly and sluggish, full of talk essentially

indicators.note: something full of a thing has that thing inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: sluggish means moving slowly

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word talk

explanation.surface: Someone looks ill and lethargic yet cannot stop chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sluggish' seems to be part of the description of a sickly person, but it supplies the outer word; 'sickly' belongs with 'Pale' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallow complexion is an unhealthy yellowish pallor, the look of someone pale and unwell.

clue.text: Friend shot after friend from Paris

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the sequence

parts.note: the French word for a friend
a shot is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A pal is gunned down following a French companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a past participle of shooting, but it is the noun meaning a try. The Spanish and French words for friend sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a pal, widely borrowed into informal English usage.

clue.text: Exhaustion of girl with it due for treatment

parts.note: lass is a common word for a young woman

indicators.note: material sent for treatment gets processed and altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl worn out and in need of medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For treatment' sounds medical, fitting the exhausted girl, but it tells you to rework only the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental weariness and lack of energy, a synonym for tiredness.

clue.text: Club offering women slight advantage

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
to have the edge is to hold a small lead

explanation.surface: A members' club gives its female members a small head start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but it is a golf club, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face, used for short, lofted shots near the green.

clue.text: Secure simple task covering line

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy to do
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Fasten down a straightforward job that involves a line.
explanation.walkthrough: A cinch is informal for an easy job, and it is the outer word here.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal or victory is to make it certain, so both verbs mean to settle something firmly.

clue.text: Manage to accommodate millions with temporary accommodation that's satisfactory

indicators.note: to accommodate is to find room for, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: to cope is to manage or get by
M is the abbreviation for million
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: An organiser housing huge crowds in makeshift shelters does an acceptable job.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is at the far end; everything before it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent work is adequate and up to the required standard, which is what satisfactory describes.

clue.text: Greek island coin redesigned

indicators.note: a thing redesigned is given a new form, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek island has had its currency given a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' seems to describe the island, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic refers to Ionia, a region of ancient Greece, and to one of the classical Greek architectural orders.

clue.text: University academic going from for to against such a priest

indicators.note: going from one thing to another describes a swap, one element replaced by its opposite

parts.note: a professor is a senior university teacher
pro means in favour of
con means opposed, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A professor switches sides and becomes a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO and CON are the two sides of an argument, so the first three letters of the academic's title flip.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessor is a priest who hears confessions and grants absolution in the Catholic church.

clue.text: College grounds American supporting faction

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever supports another thing sits beneath it

parts.note: a camp is a group sharing a position, as in the rival camps
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A US student backs one side in a college dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' can look like a verb meaning bases, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Feels sights must include extremes of Naples

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: sees, in the verb sense of sights

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A tourist feels that any view worth seeing must take in Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sights' looks like a plural noun for tourist attractions, but it is a verb meaning spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to feel or perceive it, so the third-person verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sign of tooth decay not caught

indicators.note: 'not' says something is absent, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: caries is the medical term for decay of teeth
C stands for caught on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A symptom that tooth rot was not spotted in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a symptom, but it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is the first of the twelve astrological star signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Sway and come in shaking

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles its contents, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rocks from side to side and enters trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sway' reads as a verb about rocking, but it is the noun for power or control.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have control and influence over others, which is what dominance is.

clue.text: Column on paid performer's sketch

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: a professional is paid to perform
a file is a line of people one behind another, as in single file

explanation.surface: A newspaper column carries a drawing of a professional entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests newspapers, but here it is a line of soldiers or people.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a short biographical piece or outline drawing, and a sketch can be either.

clue.text: Forgoes key cuts

parts.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: Someone skips the important reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately avoid or abstain from it, the same as doing without.

clue.text: Encourage mimic seen outside theatre at first

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to simulate is to imitate

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only the initial is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of theatre

explanation.surface: Egg on an impressionist spotted by the theatre door before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mimic' reads as a noun for an impressionist, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to spur on or rouse to action, a close synonym of the verb to encourage.

clue.text: Coverage of Sun in race for circulation

indicators.note: things put into circulation get moved around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid's reporting on a horse race, printed to boost sales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and 'coverage' and 'circulation' both play on newspapers; 'in' looks like a container signal but is just a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance provides cover against loss or damage, so a policy is also called coverage.

clue.text: A traveller mostly tells stories to find inconsistencies

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a nomad wanders from place to place
to tell stories is to lie

explanation.surface: A wanderer spins tall tales, leaving holes in the account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tells stories' is the idiom for fibbing, not narrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are deviations from what is standard or expected, things that do not fit the pattern.

clue.text: Disguises query in case of mistakes

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
a case is the outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of mistakes
to query is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone hides a question inside a file of errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Query' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to ask, which then sits inside the shell of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Masks are coverings that hide the face, and as a verb masking is hiding, both matching disguises.

clue.text: Important opus oddly written within minutes

indicators.note: what is written within something is set inside it

parts.note: moments are brief spans of time, like minutes

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and so on are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of opus

explanation.surface: A composer dashes off a major work in a matter of minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' could be meeting records, but it means short spells of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous is of great consequence, a stronger synonym for significant or weighty.

clue.text: Try relish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sample, as with food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a sauce you might try; it is a separate meaning, a fondness for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for sampling food and as a noun for a liking, as in a taste for adventure.

clue.text: Snarl, seeing no good in story

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A reader growls on finding nothing worthwhile in a narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarl' suggests a growl, but it is the noun for a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl of wool or hair is a knotted, twisted mess, the same thing as a tangle.

clue.text: Gets the better of tutors ordered to accept second degree

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another
to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
S is the abbreviation for second
a Master of Arts, a university degree

explanation.surface: Students beat their teachers, who are told to take a further qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second degree' reads as one phrase, like a postgraduate qualification, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to beat them by being cleverer, which is getting the better of them.

clue.text: Worsen a tendency to expose politicians

indicators.note: to expose is to uncover, so a word lying within the text is revealed

parts.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: An exposé on politicians only makes their bad habits worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters starts inside the first word and ends inside the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, a body made up of elected politicians or statesmen.

clue.text: Enlightenment provided by commercial transport in troubled Iran

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
something troubled is disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a van is a commercial vehicle for goods

explanation.surface: Peace of mind arrives in a delivery lorry in a country in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled Iran' paints a political picture, but it only asks for the four letters to be reshuffled around the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the state of spiritual enlightenment that ends the cycle of suffering and rebirth.

clue.text: Man for example found under a corridor

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is found under something is placed below it

parts.note: taken as written
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man is discovered beneath a passageway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but its capital marks the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, as in a church or plane, so a kind of corridor.

clue.text: Meat that could be cooked for stag party?

definitions.text: Meat that could be cooked for stag party?

parts.words: Meat that could be cooked for stag party?
parts.note: surface reading: food prepared for a groom's night out with his friends
setter's reading: the stag is the animal itself, the party whose flesh is served

explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British bachelor party before a wedding; here 'stag party' is read as the deer involved, and its meat is what gets cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of deer, including the male stag, has its own culinary name distinct from the animal.

clue.text: Struggles to accept western opinions

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to vie is to compete or strive
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: People struggle to take on board Western attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggles' reads as a verb about difficulty, but it is the verb meaning competes.
explanation.definitionFit: Views and opinions are both personal beliefs or judgements held about a matter.

clue.text: Fur buyer's source in auction

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a sale by auction

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of buyer

explanation.surface: A dealer who buys pelts at auction obtains them there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' reads as a supplier of goods, but it means the start of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark, valuable pelt of a small Asian marten, prized for coats and brushes.

clue.text: Groundbreaking victory that's overwhelming?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: earth breaking away and sliding down a slope
second meaning: an election won by a huge margin

explanation.surface: A pioneering win that swamped the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groundbreaking' normally means innovative; read literally, it is the ground itself breaking loose. The question mark flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a collapse of earth down a hillside and a crushing election win.

clue.text: Part of drill by soldiers in revolution

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece stands beside another

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
the drill bit is the part that bores the hole

explanation.surface: A section of parade-ground drilling performed by troops during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' suggests military exercise, matching the soldiers, but it is the tool. 'Revolution' looks political, yet means one circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one full circuit of a body around another, which is what a revolution means in astronomy.

clue.text: Stumbles across parking and drives off

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece stretches round another

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
P is the symbol for a car park

explanation.surface: A driver trips over a parking space, then speeds away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumbles across' looks like the idiom for finding by chance, but 'across' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attacker is to force them back or away, which is to drive them off.

clue.text: Bands of elite forces protecting the girl

indicators.note: a protector surrounds and shields what it guards, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: Special forces units are guarding a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests groups of soldiers, but it means strips of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn across the body or at the waist, a kind of band.
